name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,784

entries.clue: Conservative and liberal creep in embrace (6)

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal
to inch is to creep forward slowly

annotation.surface: Two rival parties shuffle towards each other in an awkward political hug.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'Conservative and liberal' look like a coalition; they are just two letters, and 'creep' is a verb, not a sneaky person.
annotation.definitionFit: A clinch is an embrace, as between lovers or boxers holding on.

entries.clue: Wind up Tory with hint about dire leader (8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so CLUE is placed round the D
indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of 'dire' is its first letter

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, i.e. a Tory
a clue is a hint
first letter of 'dire'

annotation.surface: Someone goads a Conservative by hinting at an awful party leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' reads as 'tease' in the surface, the natural thing to do to a Tory, but the definition means 'finish'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to wind up a meeting or speech is to bring it to a close.

entries.clue: I love pasty-looking chap in a state, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: used as is
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
wan means pale, pasty-looking

annotation.surface: Someone declares affection for a pale man who is clearly upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests agitation; here it is literal, a man from a US state. 'Perhaps' marks Iowa as just one example.
annotation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a native of Iowa, one of the US states.

entries.clue: Perfume manufacturer getting in new groove? (7)

indicatorNotes.getting in: N gets in, i.e. goes inside, CHANEL

blocks.note: Chanel, maker of No 5
N is the standard abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: A fragrance house is trying to find its fresh rhythm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groove' in the surface sounds like getting into the swing of things; it is a physical furrow. N goes after CHAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A channel is a groove or furrow cut into a surface.

entries.clue: Alpha female snorts coke of high quality (3-5)

indicatorNotes.snorts: to snort is to take something in, so TOP LASS takes in C

blocks.note: the top lass is the alpha female
C is slang for cocaine

annotation.surface: A domineering woman takes cocaine, and only the best stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has 'of high quality' describing the coke; it is the definition, and 'Alpha female' is a single idea, not two.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something of high quality is first-rate, top of its class.

entries.clue: Old worker snarfing seconds could be thus (5)

annotation.definition: Old worker snarfing seconds could be thus

indicatorNotes.snarfing: to snarf is to wolf food down, so BEE takes S inside

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a worker is a worker bee
S is the standard abbreviation for seconds

annotation.surface: An elderly employee always going back for second helpings might end up this way.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone wolfing down second helpings could well become obese. S goes inside BEE.
annotation.definitionFit: Anyone who keeps eating second helpings could become obese, which is what 'thus' points to.

entries.clue: Policeman injecting horse will get the axe (7)

indicatorNotes.injecting: COPPER injects H, putting it inside

blocks.note: a copper is a policeman
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

annotation.surface: A police officer shooting up heroin is going to be sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get the axe' reads as being fired; the definition is the axe itself. Horse is drug slang for heroin, and H is heroin's abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A chopper is an axe or cleaver, something that chops.

entries.clue: No one fart about when Hoskins gets up! (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are moved about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A plea for decorum in the bedroom when the setter finally rises.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a self-deprecating joke by the setter, Hoskins, claiming to lie in until the afternoon.
annotation.definitionFit: The setter jokingly claims not to rise until the afternoon.

entries.clue: Overindulges and goes off booty (6)

blocks.note: what doting grandparents do to a child
what milk or meat does when it turns bad
plunder taken by the victors of a war

annotation.surface: Someone eats too much and then their bottom turns bad.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions, not two: 'goes off' is a third meaning between the others. 'Booty' suggests a backside in the surface but means plunder.
annotation.definitionFit: Spoils means overindulges, goes bad, and plunder taken in war.

entries.clue: Unusual to grab head of lizard and choke (8)

indicatorNotes.to grab: STRANGE grabs the L, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.head of: the head of 'lizard' is its first letter

blocks.note: strange means unusual
first letter of 'lizard'

annotation.surface: An odd scene: someone seizes a lizard by the head and throttles it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grab' and 'choke' make the surface a single violent act, which hides that 'to grab' is only an instruction to hold a letter inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to choke someone is to throttle them by the neck.

entries.clue: Modern fortified building in English city (9)

blocks.note: new means modern
a castle is a fortified building

annotation.surface: A recently built fortress stands somewhere in England.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is almost a literal history: Newcastle upon Tyne is named after the 'new castle' built there in 1080.
annotation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in north-east England.

entries.clue: Best party, getting gone in the head! (5)

indicatorNotes.in the head: OUT is placed at the head of DO, in front of it

blocks.note: gone and out both mean away or departed
a do is a party

annotation.surface: The finest party is the one where everyone gets out of their heads.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective praising the party; it is a verb, to beat. 'Gone in the head' suggests drunkenness, but just puts OUT first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to best a rival is to beat or surpass them.

entries.clue: Story with knight stealing new bedding? (5)

indicatorNotes.stealing: LIE plus N steals the second N, taking it inside

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
N is the chess notation for knight
N is the standard abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: A tale of a knight who makes off with fresh sheets.
annotation.walkthrough: Two N's with different jobs: the knight is added to the story, and the new one is taken inside. The question mark flags that linen covers more than bedding.
annotation.definitionFit: Bed linen is bedding; the question mark admits linen is also table linen and cloth.

entries.clue: A vocal on Substitute or Out of Time? (9)

blocks.note: used as is
a temp is a substitute worker
oral and vocal both mean spoken

annotation.surface: A music quiz: is that singing on the Who's Substitute or the Stones' Out of Time?
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make both phrases song titles: Substitute by the Who and Out of Time by the Rolling Stones. Neither is a song here.
annotation.definitionFit: Atemporal means existing outside time, out of time.

entries.clue: Unfeeling member very posh girl rejected (4,3)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected means sent back, so GEL runs backwards

blocks.note: dead means very, as in 'dead easy'
gel is the posh pronunciation of girl

annotation.surface: A heartless club member turns down a very upper-class young woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unfeeling member' reads as a cold person in a club; it is a numb limb. A dead leg is a thigh numbed by a blow.
annotation.definitionFit: A dead leg is a leg, a member or limb, left numb and without feeling.

entries.clue: It's a crime to break peaceful agreement (9)

indicatorNotes.to break: the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Breaking a peace treaty would be criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a moral statement about treaties, with the anagram fodder disguised as the start of a sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a truce, like the agreement that ended fighting on 11 November 1918.

entries.clue: French main? Opening unopened wine! (6)

blocks.note: the main is the sea, which is mer in French
an opening is a SLOT; without its first letter, LOT

annotation.surface: A French main course, and a bottle of wine left uncorked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like a main course; it is the old word for the open sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Merlot is one red grape variety and its wine.

entries.clue: Thin Frenchman with brilliant speed (8)

blocks.note: M is short for Monsieur
ace means brilliant
rate means speed

annotation.surface: A skinny Frenchman who is dazzlingly fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thin' reads as an adjective describing the Frenchman; it is a verb. To macerate is also, less commonly, to make or grow thin.
annotation.definitionFit: Macerate can mean to cause to waste away or grow thin, as well as to soften by soaking.

entries.clue: Ring roads close to old-fashioned school (8)

blocks.note: by means near, close to
passé means out of date
S is the standard abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: Roads loop round near an outdated school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring roads' looks like an instruction to circle roads; it is the definition. A British ring road circles a town, as a bypass skirts one.
annotation.definitionFit: Bypasses are roads that take traffic round a town, like ring roads.

entries.clue: Hoskins is dim prick all the way through! (6)

blocks.note: the setter speaking says I'M
pale means dim, faint

annotation.surface: The setter owns up to being a stupid idiot, totally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dim prick' reads as an insult the setter aims at himself; 'dim' goes with the wordplay and 'prick' starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce right through with a spike.

entries.clue: A wine opened by old American gets you excited (7)

indicatorNotes.opened by: RED is opened up and OUS is put inside

blocks.note: used as is
red is wine
O is the standard abbreviation for old
US is short for American

annotation.surface: Uncorking a bottle with an elderly American puts you in high spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has an old American opening the wine; in the wordplay the wine itself is opened up and the old American goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: excited in the sense of stirred up or roused.

entries.clue: Londoner likely to knock Hoskins's head off? (7)

annotation.definition: Londoner likely to knock Hoskins's head off?

blocks.note: the definition proper: a particular kind of Londoner

blocks.clueFragment: likely to knock Hoskins's head off?
blocks.note: reads as a threat of violence; really it means dropping the H at the front of the setter's name

annotation.surface: A threat from a violent East Ender to beat up the setter.
annotation.walkthrough: The threat of violence is a decoy: a Cockney, a working-class East Londoner, drops the H at the start of words, knocking the head off 'Hoskins'.
annotation.definitionFit: A Cockney is an East Londoner, famous for dropping initial aitches.

entries.clue: Is it possible that adolescent is a mess? (7)

blocks.note: 'can' asks whether it is possible, as in 'Can it be?'
a teen is an adolescent

annotation.surface: A parent wonders whether their teenager can really be this untidy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A mess' reads as untidiness; it is a place where soldiers eat, and a canteen is exactly that.
annotation.definitionFit: A mess is a military dining room, which is a canteen.

entries.clue: Dodgy bloke, one Edwina worried about? (3,3)

blocks.note: idiom for a rogue or ne'er-do-well
Edwina Currie warned of salmonella in eggs

annotation.surface: Edwina is anxious about a suspicious man.
annotation.walkthrough: In 1988 the British health minister Edwina Currie caused a scandal by saying most British eggs carried salmonella; the question mark flags the topical allusion.
annotation.definitionFit: A bad egg is a rogue, and a literal bad egg was what Edwina Currie worried about.

entries.clue: One who legs it if Rob dances badly (9)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are arranged badly, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone flees the dance floor when Rob starts his terrible moves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like theft to go with 'legs it', but it is just a name supplying letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An absconder is someone who runs away, who legs it.

entries.clue: Leader of DUP having sex is quaintly comical (5)

indicatorNotes.Leader of: the leader of 'DUP' is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of 'DUP'
a roll in the hay is sex

annotation.surface: The head of a Northern Irish party caught in bed is faintly ridiculous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader of DUP' tempts a real politician; it only means D. The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
annotation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in an odd or quaint way.

entries.clue: Sleep for short while with old man in leather (5)

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep
pa is father, one's old man

annotation.surface: Dad dozes off briefly in his leather armchair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container indicator, but it only links the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Nappa is a soft leather made from sheepskin or lambskin.

entries.clue: Vacuous police surrounding free festival (5)

indicatorNotes.Vacuous: vacuous means empty, so 'police' keeps only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround something is to enclose it, so the PE letters go around RID

blocks.note: outer letters of 'police'
to rid is to free

annotation.surface: Brainless police officers ring a festival that costs nothing to attend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free festival' reads as a no-cost event; 'free' is a verb giving RID. RID goes between P and E.
annotation.definitionFit: Pride is the annual LGBTQ+ festival and march.

entries.clue: Sinful things produced by out-of-head fiends (5)

indicatorNotes.out-of-head: DEVILS is out of its head, losing its first letter

blocks.note: fiends are DEVILS; the head letter D goes

annotation.surface: Wicked deeds committed by demons who are off their faces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-head' looks like drug slang for high; it means the first letter goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sins and wrongdoings are evils.

entries.clue: Drinking booze? So then sip to get drunk! (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.to get drunk: drunk letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone decides the next step is to drink until drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all about drinking, and so is the answer: 'on the piss' is British slang for out drinking heavily.
annotation.definitionFit: On the piss is British slang for out on a heavy drinking session.

entries.clue: Girl eyed criminal in a rapacious way (8)

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters are criminally misused, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A young woman looks over a crook with an acquisitive gleam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, the thing the girl eyed; it is an adjective signalling the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Greedily means rapaciously, grabbing more than one's share.

entries.clue: A northern set with southern backers (6)

blocks.note: used as is
N is the standard abbreviation for northern
jelly sets, or gels
S is the standard abbreviation for southern

annotation.surface: A group from the North has some supporters from the South.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun, a group; it is a verb. Angels are investors who fund stage shows.
annotation.definitionFit: Angels are financial backers, especially of theatre productions.
